page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a virtual machine instance from the Lasv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 960 GB drive, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory subsystem performance shows a notable bottleneck, with both small-block and large-block read-only memory bandwidth testing in the bottom 25%, though large-block write bandwidth remains average. Computational tasks such as text processing score in the top 25%, while software compilation with Clang and database operations on Passmark fall into the bottom 25%. Large language model inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to poor or weak tiers for medium 7B models.

The L4as_v4 instance offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring a high memory footprint relative to compute cores, combined with local storage capacity. Given the weak read-only memory bandwidth and lower multi-threaded decompression performance, it is less suited for memory-bound high-performance computing or heavy database operations. Instead, the hardware profile and benchmark results suggest a fit for single-threaded applications, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight containerized workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and local storage without requiring high-throughput memory access.
